questions.question: A salesman marks his good 84% above the cost price and gives a discount of 50% on them. Find the percentage of this gain or loss.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net Profit or Loss percentage can be calculated using the **Successive Percentage** formula: a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100.

Here, a = 84 (Markup percentage) and b = −50 (Discount percentage).

Net effect = 84 − 50 + (84 × (−50)) ÷ 100.

Net effect = 34 − 4200 ÷ 100 = 34 − 42 = −8%.

The negative sign indicates a **loss** of 8%.

**∴ The correct answer is 8% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Markup % = 84%, Discount % = 50%.

**Formulas:** MP = CP × (100 + Markup%) ÷ 100 | SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100 | Loss% = (CP − SP) ÷ CP × 100.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0723b647d823dbdc723bba71ff8d241d06ee4b32275f95099d65084887b735c7.png] 

⇒ Let the **Cost Price (CP)** be 100.

⇒ **Marked Price (MP)** = 100 + 84% of 100 = 184.

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 184 − 50% of 184 = 184 − 92 = 92.

⇒ **Loss** = CP − SP = 100 − 92 = 8.

⇒ **Loss %** = (8 ÷ 100) × 100 = 8%.

**∴ The correct answer is 8% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and Discount

The price listed on the label is the **Marked Price**. Discount is always calculated on the MP to arrive at the **Selling Price**.

MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%). This helps find any one value if the other three are known.</p

questions.question: A man has to cover a distance of 549 km in 8 hours. If he covers (2)/(3)of this distance in (3)/(4)of the time, then what should be his speed (in km/hr) to cover the remaining distance in the time left?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__
Remaining distance = (1 − 2/3) × 549 = 1/3 × 549 = 183 km.

Remaining time = (1 − 3/4) × 8 = 1/4 × 8 = 2 hours.

Required Speed = Remaining Distance ÷ Remaining Time = 183 ÷ 2 = 91.5 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 91.5 km/hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Total distance = 549 km, Total time = 8 hours.

**Formula Used:** Speed = Distance ÷ Time
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aa0ae280174d836288683ee7ba73e1bc3fca35bf9c89d8d7e01eb9c75490fe0d.png] 
⇒ **Distance covered** = 2/3 × 549 = 366 km

⇒ **Remaining distance** = 549 − 366 = 183 km

⇒ **Time taken** = 3/4 × 8 = 6 hours

⇒ **Remaining time** = 8 − 6 = 2 hours

⇒ **Required Speed** = 183 ÷ 2 = 91.5 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 91.5 km/hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. If distances are equal, Average Speed = 2xy/(x+y).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

Relative Speed

Same direction = S₁ − S₂ | Opposite direction = S₁ + S₂.</p

questions.question: Which two policy areas are explicitly managed by the Union Cabinet in India as part of its coordinating functions?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Foreign Relations and Defence**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Union Cabinet** in India explicitly manages **Foreign Relations** and **Defence** as part of its coordinating functions.
 
• Under **Article 73** of the Indian Constitution, the Union Government has exclusive powers to legislate on matters relating to **foreign affairs** and **defence.**
 
• **Foreign Relations** involve managing India’s diplomatic ties, treaties, trade agreements, and coordination with international organizations such as the **United Nations**.
 
• **Defence** encompasses the responsibility of ensuring national security, managing the armed forces (Army, Navy, and Air Force), and overseeing strategic operations.
 
• The Union Cabinet handles critical decisions such as signing international treaties, defense procurement, and deploying forces during crises.
 
• These areas are fundamental to maintaining the sovereignty, security, and global standing of India, which is why they are explicitly managed by the central government.
 
• The Ministry of **External Affairs** and the Ministry of **Defence** work in coordination with the Union Cabinet to implement policies in these domains.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Agriculture and Labour**__

 __
 
• **Agriculture** falls under the **State List** as per the Constitution of India, meaning that state governments primarily manage policies related to agriculture.
 
• **Labour** is included in the **Concurrent List**, which allows both the Union and State Governments to legislate on issues such as employment, wages, and industrial disputes.
 
• The Union Cabinet does intervene in labour matters for national-level policies, but these are not exclusively managed by the Union Cabinet.
 
 
 
• **Tourism and Sports**__
 __
 
• **Tourism** is primarily managed by the states, though the Union Government promotes national-level tourism campaigns and policies like **Incredible India**.
 
• **Sports** policies and development programs are largely coordinated by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, but these do not fall under the exclusive domain of the Union Cabinet.
 
 
 
• **Education and Health**__
 
 
• **Education** is part of the **Concurrent List**, and both Union and State Governments can legislate on matters related to schools, universities, and other educational institutions.
 
• **Health** is also in the **State List**, meaning state governments have primary responsibility for healthcare policies, though the Union Government coordinates national health schemes like **Ayushman Bharat**.

questions.question: 3 men and 14 women can complete a piece of work in 18 days, and 11 men and 8 women can complete the same work in 12 days. The work of how many women is equivalent to that of one man?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__
Equate **Total Work**: (3M + 14W) × 18 = (11M + 8W) × 12

Divide both sides by 6: (3M + 14W) × 3 = (11M + 8W) × 2

9M + 42W = 22M + 16W

26W = 13M ⇒ 2W = 1M

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Case 1: **3 Men** and **14 Women** in **18 days**.

Case 2: **11 Men** and **8 Women** in **12 days**.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = (Number of workers × Time taken)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Work = (3M + 14W) × 18 --- (i)

⇒ Total Work = (11M + 8W) × 12 --- (ii)

⇒ (3M + 14W) × 18 = (11M + 8W) × 12

⇒ 3(3M + 14W) = 2(11M + 8W)

⇒ 9M + 42W = 22M + 16W

⇒ 42W − 16W = 22M − 9M

⇒ 26W = 13M

⇒ 1M = 2W

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

**__Additional Information__**

Man-Day Concept

Total work is constant and expressed as the product of efficiency and time. M₁D₁ = M₂D₂.

Work and Wages

Wages are distributed based on the ratio of work done, which is often the ratio of efficiencies when time is constant.</p

questions.question: In which landmark case did the Supreme Court of India rule that the Council of Ministers DOES NOT cease to hold office even after the dissolution of the Lok Sabha?

options.text: Kesavananda Bharati vs. State of Kerala, 1973
SR Bommai vs. Union of India, 1994

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**UNR Rao vs. Indira Gandhi, 1971**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The case of **UNR Rao vs. Indira Gandhi, 1971**, is a landmark judgment by the **Supreme Court of India**.
 
• In this case, the court ruled that the **Council of Ministers** does not cease to hold office even after the **dissolution of the Lok Sabha**.
 
• This judgment clarified that the Council of Ministers continues to function and assist the **President of India** in discharging their duties.
 
• The decision was based on the interpretation of **Article 74 of the Indian Constitution**, which provides for a Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister to aid and advise the President.
 
• This case established that the executive authority of the government does not come to a standstill with the dissolution of the Lok Sabha, ensuring continuity in governance.
 
• It highlights the importance of the principle of **collective responsibility** of the Council of Ministers to the Lok Sabha, as enshrined in the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kesavananda Bharati vs. State of Kerala, 1973**__

 __
 
• This case is famous for the **Basic Structure Doctrine**, which limits the power of Parliament to amend the Constitution.
 
• The court ruled that while Parliament can amend any part of the Constitution, it cannot alter its **basic structure**.
 
• This case is considered a cornerstone in the history of **Indian constitutional law**.
 
 
 
• **Golaknath vs. State of Punjab, 1967**__
 __
 
• This case ruled that **Fundamental Rights** cannot be amended by Parliament.
 
• It declared that the Constitution's **Fundamental Rights** were sacrosanct and inviolable.
 
• However, this decision was later overturned by the Kesavananda Bharati case.
 
 
 
• **SR Bommai vs. Union of India, 1994**__
 
 
• This case is a landmark judgment in the context of the **President's Rule** under Article 356 of the Constitution.
 
• The court laid down the principles of judicial review of the imposition of **President's Rule**.
 
• It emphasized that the **secular character of the Constitution** is part of its basic structure.

questions.question: Find the smallest number by which 4232 must be multiplied to make it a perfect square.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Perform prime factorization of **4232**.

4232 = 2 × 2116 = 2 × 2 × 1058 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 529 = 2³ × 23²

Grouping into pairs: (2 × 2) × 2 × (23 × 23).

Only one **2** is left without a pair, so we must multiply by **2**.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given number is **4232**.

To find the smallest number to multiply to make it a **perfect square**, we use the **prime factorization method**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/eb4cd647d682f8729a0432f78e6dad6a983b894773079cba1267dd2dde750a8c.png] 

⇒ Prime factors of 4232 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 23 × 23

⇒ Grouping the prime factors in identical pairs: (2 × 2) × (23 × 23) × 2

⇒ The prime factor **2** does not have a pair.

⇒ Therefore, 4232 must be multiplied by **2** to make it a perfect square.

⇒ New number = 4232 × 2 = 8464 (which is 92²)

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

**__Additional Information__**

Perfect Square Property

In the prime factorization of any perfect square, the exponent of every prime factor must be an even number.

Division Rule for Perfect Squares

The smallest number by which a number must be divided to make it a perfect square is also the unpaired factor (which is 2 in this case).</p

questions.question: The royal title used by Chandragupta I was:
questions.solution:

__
 
• Chandragupta I was the **founder of the Gupta Empire** and reigned during the early 4th century CE.
 
• He adopted the title of **"Maharajadhiraja,"** meaning "**King of Kings**," to signify his authority over other rulers and his elevated status.
 
• The use of this title marked the **rise of the Gupta Empire** as a prominent and centralized political power in ancient India.
 
• This designation highlighted the **imperial ambitions** of Chandragupta I, as he sought to consolidate power and unify regions under his rule.
 
• The title "Maharajadhiraja" had been used by other rulers in ancient India, but its adoption by Chandragupta I signified the **beginning of the Gupta dynasty's golden age.**
 
• Under Chandragupta I's reign, the Gupta Empire expanded its influence, particularly in the **Magadha region**, which was a significant center of power.
 
• This era is considered a period of **political stability, economic prosperity, and cultural advancements,** laying the foundation for the Gupta Empire's future achievements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Maharaj**__

 __
 
• The term **"Maharaj"** simply means "great king" but does not carry the same imperial connotation as "Maharajadhiraja."
 
• It was commonly used by rulers, including those who governed smaller kingdoms or regions, during ancient Indian history.
 
 
 
• **Chakravartin**__
 __
 
• The term **"Chakravartin"** refers to a "universal ruler" or someone who rules ethically and universally over the known world.
 
• It was a title often associated with rulers who adhered to **Dharmic principles** and was more symbolic than political.
 
• This title was not specifically used by Chandragupta I.
 
 
 
• **Samrat**__
 
 
• The title **"Samrat"** means "emperor" and was used by rulers to denote supreme authority.
 
• While it is similar to "Maharajadhiraja," Chandragupta I specifically chose the latter to emphasize his superiority over other kings.

questions.question: If a² + b² = 163, a times b = 27 { and } a > b, then find the value of (a - b)/(a + b)
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

To find (a − b) / (a + b), we use the square identities: (a − b)² = (a² + b²) − 2ab and (a + b)² = (a² + b²) + 2ab.

Numerator value: (a − b)² = 163 − 2(27) = 163 − 54 = 109.

Denominator value: (a + b)² = 163 + 2(27) = 163 + 54 = 217.

Taking the square root of both sides: (a − b) / (a + b) = √109 / √217 = √(109/217).

**∴ The correct answer is √(109/217).**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

a² + b² = 163

a × b = 27

a > b

**Formula Used:**

1. (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

2. (a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a24dab41a7fe8fa1c933d9a93aea165272e8ef1a2a72e5288f474eee3925d436.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2ab = 2 × 27 = 54

⇒ (a + b)² = 163 + 54 = 217

⇒ a + b = √217 (Since a > b, sum is positive)

⇒ (a − b)² = 163 − 54 = 109

⇒ a − b = √109 (Since a > b, difference is positive)

⇒ (a − b) / (a + b) = √109 / √217

⇒ (a − b) / (a + b) = √(109 / 217)

**∴ The correct answer is √(109/217).**

**__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Expansion of Square of Sum

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab. This identity links the sum of squares, the product of terms, and the square of the sum.

Algebraic Expansion of Square of Difference

(a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab. This is used to find the difference between two variables when their squares and product are known.

Difference of Two Squares

a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b). This is a fundamental factoring identity used to simplify fractional algebraic expressions.</p

questions.question:
For which of the given bills can the President of India summon a joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament?

1. Ordinary Bill

2. Money Bill

3. Constitutional Amendment Bill
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**1 only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **President of India** can summon a **joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament** under **Article 108** of the Constitution.
 
• This is applicable in cases of a legislative deadlock on an **Ordinary Bill**, where both Houses fail to agree on its passage.
 
• A joint sitting is presided over by the **Speaker of the Lok Sabha**, or in their absence, the Deputy Speaker.
 
• Joint sittings are convened to resolve disputes between the **Lok Sabha** and **Rajya Sabha** concerning an Ordinary Bill.
 
• The **Money Bill** and **Constitutional Amendment Bill** are excluded from this provision as they have distinct procedural requirements and do not fall under legislative deadlock scenarios.
 
• The joint sitting mechanism reflects the principle of resolving conflicts and ensuring the smooth functioning of the legislative process in a parliamentary democracy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Money Bill**__

 __
 
• A **Money Bill** is specifically defined under **Article 110** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It primarily deals with matters related to the **imposition, abolition, remission, alteration, or regulation of taxes**, borrowing of money, expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India, etc.
 
• The **Lok Sabha** has exclusive power to approve a Money Bill, while the **Rajya Sabha** can only recommend changes within a limited timeframe.
 
• No provision for a joint sitting exists for Money Bills, as the Lok Sabha holds greater authority in financial matters.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Amendment Bill**__
 
 
• A **Constitutional Amendment Bill** is governed under **Article 368** of the Constitution.
 
• Such bills are passed with a special majority in both Houses of Parliament, and there is no provision for a joint sitting to resolve differences.
 
• These bills often require ratification by at least half of the **State Legislatures** for amendments impacting the federal structure.
 
• The procedural requirements for Constitutional Amendment Bills are distinct from Ordinary Bills and Money Bills.

questions.question: Which of the following memory types is also called solid-state storage?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Flash Memory**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Flash Memory** is a type of **non-volatile storage**, meaning it retains data even when the power is turned off.
 
• It is often referred to as **solid-state storage** because it has no moving parts, unlike traditional hard drives.
 
• This memory is widely used in devices such as **USB flash drives, memory cards, solid-state drives (SSDs),** and various embedded systems.
 
• It is based on **NAND or NOR flash technology**, which uses floating-gate transistors to store data.
 
• Flash memory is known for its **high speed, durability, and compact size**, making it suitable for modern computing and mobile devices.
 
• It enables the storage of data in **a rewritable format**, allowing users to repeatedly write and erase data.
 
• Flash memory is also highly energy-efficient compared to other storage technologies, making it ideal for portable devices.
 
• Common applications include **smartphones, tablets, cameras, and solid-state drives (SSDs)** in computers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Cache Memory**__

 __
 
• **Cache Memory** is a high-speed memory that temporarily stores frequently accessed data for quick retrieval.
 
• It is located closer to the CPU and is used to improve **processing speed**.
 
• Cache memory is not considered solid-state storage because it is volatile and does not retain data when power is off.
 
 
 
• **Crystal Storage**__
 __
 
• **Crystal Storage** refers to experimental data storage technologies using crystals, such as **quartz glass**.
 
• It is not widely implemented and is different from flash memory.
 
 
 
• **Primary Memory**__
 
 
• **Primary Memory**, also known as **main memory**, includes **RAM** and ROM.
 
• It is volatile in the case of RAM and does not qualify as solid-state storage.
 
• ROM, while non-volatile, is not rewritable like flash memory.

questions.question: A sum, when invested at 20% simple interest per annum, amounts to ₹4,800 after 3 years. What is the simple interest (in ₹) on the same sum at the same rate in 1 year?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total interest percentage for **3 years** at **20%** = 20% × 3 = **60%**.

Total amount percentage = **Principal (100%)** + **Interest (60%)** = **160%**.

Given: 160% = **₹4,800** ⇒ 1% = 4800 ÷ 160 = **₹30**.

Interest for **1 year** at 20% = 20 × 30 = **₹600**.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Amount (A) = **₹4,800**, Rate (R) = **20% p.a.**, Time (T) = **3 years**.

**Formula Used:** Amount (A) = P + SI = P + (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aac82e86215a1adf686fd936417f8bf15d857f0a0c13c48f6d9c5ef5953f178a.png] 

⇒ 4,800 = P × (1 + (20 × 3) ÷ 100)

⇒ 4,800 = P × (1 + 0.6)

⇒ 4,800 = P × 1.6

⇒ P = 4,800 ÷ 1.6 = **₹3,000**

⇒ Simple Interest for 1 year = (3000 × 20 × 1) ÷ 100

⇒ Simple Interest = 30 × 20 = **₹600**

**∴ The correct answer is ₹600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest (SI) formula

SI is calculated only on the **Principal** amount: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100, where P is principal, R is rate per annum, and T is time in years.

Amount in Simple Interest

The total **Amount (A)** is the sum of the Principal and Simple Interest: A = P + SI = P(1 + RT/100).

Annual Interest Constant

In Simple Interest, the interest earned remains **constant every year** because it is always calculated on the original principal.

Total Volume = Volume of **Cube** + Volume of **Cuboid**

Total Volume = 5³ + (35 × 15 × 15) = 125 + 7875 = 8000 cm³

Number of new cubes = Total Volume ÷ Volume of **New Cube**

Number of new cubes = 8000 ÷ 10³ = 8000 ÷ 1000 = 8

**∴ The correct answer is 8 cubes.**

⇒ Volume of one new cube = 10 × 10 × 10 = 1000 cm³

⇒ Number of cubes = Total Volume ÷ Volume of one new cube

⇒ Number of cubes = 8000 ÷ 1000 = 8

**∴ The correct answer is 8 cubes.**

Conservation of Volume

When one or more solid objects are **melted** and recast into new shapes, the total **volume remains constant**.

• This issue was significant as it highlighted the growing nationalist sentiment and dissatisfaction with British policies that excluded Indians from key roles in governance.
 
• The Bombay Session was presided over by **W.C. Bonnerjee**, the first president of the INC, and laid the foundation for subsequent sessions to address various political and economic grievances.
 
• The demand for Indianisation of administrative services became a recurring theme in the early years of the INC and reflected the aspirations of educated Indians for equal opportunities under British rule.

questions.question: What does 'Dhamma' primarily refer to in Ashoka’s inscriptions?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Moral law**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **'Dhamma'**, as used in **Ashoka's inscriptions**, primarily refers to a set of **ethical and moral principles** that were intended to guide the behavior of individuals and the administration of the state.
 
• This concept of Dhamma was not limited to **Buddhist teachings** but was a broader moral code aimed at promoting **social harmony, tolerance, and non-violence**.
 
• The Dhamma included principles such as **respect for elders, compassion towards all living beings, non-violence (Ahimsa), and truthfulness**.
 
• Ashoka, after embracing **Buddhism**, adopted these moral principles and propagated them through his **edicts**, which were inscribed on rocks and pillars across his empire.
 
• The inscriptions reflect Ashoka's efforts to create a just and ethical society by emphasizing the importance of **moral conduct** over rituals and ceremonies.
 
• Ashoka’s Dhamma was not sectarian; it was designed to be universally acceptable, addressing the welfare of all people, including animals.
 
• The promotion of Dhamma was a key part of Ashoka's efforts to govern his empire based on the principles of **righteousness** and **justice**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Slogans of Buddha**__

 __
 
• This option refers to the teachings or sayings of **Buddha**, which are known as **Dhammapada** or other Buddhist scriptures. However, Ashoka's Dhamma was broader than just Buddhist slogans; it was a universal moral code.
 
 
 
• **Royal decree**__
 __
 
• While Ashoka's inscriptions can be considered as **royal decrees**, the term 'Dhamma' specifically refers to the **ethical and moral principles** promoted through these decrees.
 
 
 
• **Buddhist doctrine**__
 
 
• Though Ashoka was a follower of **Buddhism**, his concept of Dhamma was not confined to Buddhist doctrine. It was a more inclusive and universal set of principles.

Count the total number of observations, **n = 11** (which is an **odd number**).

Arrange the data in **ascending order**: 16, 27, 32, 38, 41, 47, 67, 74, 85, 88, 98.

For odd **n**, the **Median** is the middle term: ((n + 1) ÷ 2)th term.

Median = (12 ÷ 2)th term = **6th term** = 47.

**∴ The correct answer is 47.**

⇒ Total number of observations (n) = 11

⇒ Arranging the data in **ascending order**: 16, 27, 32, 38, 41, 47, 67, 74, 85, 88, 98

⇒ Median = ((11 + 1) ÷ 2)th term

If **n** is even, the **Median** is the arithmetic mean of the (n/2)th and (n/2 + 1)th terms after arranging the data in order.

Mode

questions.question: The sides (in cm) of a right triangle are (x - 5), (x - 10) and x. Its area (in cm²) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a **Right-Angled Triangle**, the sides often follow standard **Pythagorean Triplets**.

Given sides: (x − 10), (x − 5), and x. These represent sides with a constant difference of 5.

The only standard triplet with a constant difference is 3 : 4 : 5. Multiplying by 5, we get 15 : 20 : 25.

Check: 25 − 10 = 15 and 25 − 5 = 20. Thus, x = 25, Base = 15, Height = 20.

Area = 1/2 × Base × Height = 1/2 × 15 × 20 = 150 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 150 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Sides of right triangle are (x − 10), (x − 5) and x.

**Formula Used:** **Pythagoras Theorem**: a² + b² = c², where c is the **hypotenuse** (longest side).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ecb263ceaa4082e542082a2edbee714270cd2af897ff268b00054962358eb2d2.png] 

⇒ (x − 10)² + (x − 5)² = x²

⇒ (x² − 20x + 100) + (x² − 10x + 25) = x²

⇒ 2x² − 30x + 125 = x²

⇒ x² − 30x + 125 = 0

⇒ x² − 25x − 5x + 125 = 0

⇒ x(x − 25) − 5(x − 25) = 0

⇒ (x − 25)(x − 5) = 0

⇒ x = 25 or x = 5 (x=5 not possible as side x−5 would be 0 and x−10 would be negative)

⇒ Sides are: 25, (25−5)=20, (25−10)=15

⇒ Area = 1/2 × 15 × 20 = 150 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 150 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Triplets

Sets of three integers that satisfy a² + b² = c², such as (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), and (8, 15, 17).

Area of Right Triangle

Area is calculated as 1/2 × base × height, where base and height are the two legs forming the 90° angle.

Hypotenuse Property

The hypotenuse is always the longest side of a right-angled triangle and is opposite the right angle.</p

questions.question: An article’s cost price is ₹285, and the marked price is mentioned as ₹1,140. What is the profit percentage of the seller if he sells it by allowing a discount of 70% on the marked price?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given **Cost Price (CP)** = ₹285 and **Marked Price (MP)** = ₹1,140.

The ratio of CP to MP is 285 : 1140 = 1 : 4.

If MP = 100 units, then CP = 25 units.

**Selling Price (SP)** at 70% discount = 100 − 70 = 30 units.

Profit% = (SP − CP) ÷ CP × 100 = (30 − 25) ÷ 25 × 100 = 5 ÷ 25 × 100 = 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: **Cost Price (CP)** = ₹285, **Marked Price (MP)** = ₹1,140, **Discount** = 70%.

Formulas: SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100 | Profit% = (SP − CP) ÷ CP × 100.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/20b1bee1d9f4d21d4b96062155810f830dd29e2c57bcdaf1c4fa7822f6c0ba5d.png] 

⇒ Step 1: Calculate **Selling Price (SP)** = 1140 × (100 − 70) ÷ 100

⇒ SP = 1140 × 30 ÷ 100 = 114 × 3 = ₹342

⇒ Step 2: Calculate **Profit** = SP − CP = 342 − 285 = ₹57

⇒ Step 3: Calculate **Profit Percentage** = (57 ÷ 285) × 100

questions.question: In a class of 30 students, the average score on a test is 75. If 20 students scored an average of 80, what is the average score of the remaining 10 students?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The **overall average** of 30 students is 75.

The first **20 students** have an average of 80, which is +5 more than the **total average**.

Total excess score = 20 × 5 = +100.

To balance this, the remaining **10 students** must have a total deficit of −100.

Average of remaining 10 students = 75 + (−100 ÷ 10) = 65.

**∴ The correct answer is 65.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total number of **students** = 30

Average score of **class** = 75

Average score of **20 students** = 80

**Formula Used:**

Sum of values = Average × Number of observations

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total score of all 30 students = 30 × 75 = 2250

⇒ Total score of 20 students = 20 × 80 = 1600

⇒ Total score of remaining 10 students = 2250 − 1600 = 650

⇒ Average score of remaining 10 students = 650 ÷ 10 = 65

**∴ The correct answer is 65.**

**__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Formula

When two groups with averages a₁ and a₂ and sizes n₁ and n₂ are combined, the new average is (n₁a₁ + n₂a₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Net Deviation Rule

The sum of the **deviations** of all items in a set from their **arithmetic mean** is always zero.

Constant Change

questions.question: The length, breadth and height of a cuboid are (2x - 5y + 3) m, (5x + 7y - 7) m, and (x + y + 3) m, respectively. Find the perimeter of the cuboid.

Sum of terms = (2x + 5x + x) + (−5y + 7y + y) + (3 − 7 + 3) = 8x + 3y − 1

Perimeter = 4 × (8x + 3y − 1) = 32x + 12y − 4

**∴ The correct answer is (32x + 12y − 4) m.**

⇒ Sum = 8x + 3y − 1

⇒ Perimeter = 4 × (8x + 3y − 1)

⇒ Perimeter = 32x + 12y − 4

questions.question: What happens if a no‑confidence motion is passed in the Indian Lok Sabha against the union government?

options.text: The Prime Minister is given a chance to reorganise the Cabinet.
The entire Council of Ministers must resign.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**The entire Council of Ministers must resign.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **No-Confidence Motion** is a parliamentary motion moved against the **Union Government**, indicating that the ruling government no longer holds the confidence of the majority of members in the **Lok Sabha**, as per **Article 75(3)** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• If the motion is passed, it leads to a loss of majority for the ruling government in the Lok Sabha, thereby mandating the resignation of the **entire Council of Ministers, including the Prime Minister.**
 
• The **Prime Minister** and the Council of Ministers collectively hold office during the pleasure of the President, but this is contingent upon the government maintaining the confidence of the Lok Sabha.
 
• It is a crucial legislative mechanism to ensure the accountability of the government to the elected representatives of the people.
 
• Once the Council of Ministers resigns, the President may invite the leader of another party or coalition that can prove majority support to form the new government, or may call for fresh **general elections.**
 
• The process of a No-Confidence Motion ensures the stability and democratic functioning of India's parliamentary system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Prime Minister is given a chance to reorganise the Cabinet.**__

 __
 
• This option is incorrect because a No-Confidence Motion does not provide the Prime Minister with an opportunity to reorganize the Cabinet. Instead, the motion directly challenges the authority and legitimacy of the entire government.
 
• The motion signifies loss of majority support, making it mandatory for the entire Council of Ministers to resign.
 
 
 
• **Only the dissenting ministers resign.**__
 __
 
• In the parliamentary system, the Council of Ministers functions as a collective entity. Hence, resignation due to a No-Confidence Motion applies to the **entire Council of Ministers**, not just dissenting members.
 
• Individual resignations do not address the fundamental issue of lack of majority support in the Lok Sabha.
 
 
 
• **A re-election is triggered.**__
 
 
• While a No-Confidence Motion may eventually lead to fresh elections, it is not an automatic outcome of the motion being passed.
 
• The President can invite another party or coalition with a proven majority in the Lok Sabha to form the government before considering general elections.

questions.question: A person who spends 32% of his monthly income is able to save ₹7,752 per month. His monthly expenses (in ₹) are:

**Savings** percentage = 100% − 32% = 68%

68% of **Income** = ₹7,752

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,648.**

questions.question: If the quadratic equations 6x ^ 2 - 7x - 20 = 0 and 6x ^ 2 + bx - 10 = 0 have one root in common, find the value of b.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Factorize the first equation **6x² − 7x − 20 = 0** to find its roots.

The roots are **x = 5/2** and **x = −4/3** by splitting the middle term (−15, 8).

Substitute **x = 5/2** into the second equation **6x² + bx − 10 = 0**.

6(5/2)² + b(5/2) − 10 = 0 ⇒ 37.5 + 2.5b − 10 = 0 ⇒ 2.5b = −27.5 ⇒ **b = −11**.

**∴ The correct answer is -11.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Quadratic equations **6x² − 7x − 20 = 0** and **6x² + bx − 10 = 0** have one **common root**.

**Formula Used:**

For a quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0, roots can be found by **factorization**.

**Calculations:**

First, solving **6x² − 7x − 20 = 0**:

⇒ 6x² − 15x + 8x − 20 = 0

⇒ 3x(2x − 5) + 4(2x − 5) = 0

⇒ (3x + 4)(2x − 5) = 0

⇒ **x = 5/2** or **x = −4/3**

Since the equations have one root in common, we test these values in the second equation **6x² + bx − 10 = 0**.

Case 1: Let the common root be **x = 5/2**.

⇒ 6(5/2)² + b(5/2) − 10 = 0

⇒ 6 × (25/4) + 2.5b − 10 = 0

⇒ 1.5 × 25 + 2.5b − 10 = 0

⇒ 37.5 + 2.5b − 10 = 0

⇒ 27.5 + 2.5b = 0

⇒ 2.5b = −27.5

⇒ **b = −11**

Case 2: Let the common root be **x = −4/3**.

⇒ 6(−4/3)² + b(−4/3) − 10 = 0 ⇒ 6(16/9) − 4b/3 − 10 = 0

⇒ 32/3 − 4b/3 − 10 = 0 ⇒ 2 − 4b = 0 ⇒ b = 0.5 (Not in options).

**∴ The correct answer is -11.**

**__Additional Information__**

Condition for One Common Root

For equations a₁x² + b₁x + c₁ = 0 and a₂x² + b₂x + c₂ = 0, if α is the common root, then (a₁c₂ − a₂c₁)² = (b₁c₂ − b₂c₁)(a₁b₂ − a₂b₁).

Sum and Product of Roots

For any quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0, the sum of roots is **−b/a** and the product of roots is **c/a**.

Discriminant and Nature of Roots

The nature of roots is determined by **D = b² − 4ac**. If D ≥ 0, roots are real; if D < 0, roots are imaginary.</p

• Such pairs are critical in understanding the behavior of acids and bases in chemical reactions, particularly in the context of the **Brønsted-Lowry theory.**

Time ratio (Initial : New) = 20 : 15 = 4 : 3

Speed ratio (Initial : New) = 3 : 4

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Speed (S₁) = 66 km/hr, Initial Time (T₁) = 20 hours, New Time (T₂) = 15 hours.

**__Additional Information__**

Inverse Variation in Speed and Time

When the distance to be covered is constant, the ratio of speeds is the **reciprocal** of the ratio of time taken: S₁/S₂ = T₂/T₁.

Average Speed Formula

For a round trip or same distance covered at two different speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.</p

questions.question: If sin A = 3/4 then calculate cosA cotA.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Given **sin A** = 3/4 (Perpendicular/Hypotenuse)

Base = √(4² − 3²) = √(16 − 9) = √7

**cos A** = Base/Hypotenuse = √7/4

**cot A** = Base/Perpendicular = √7/3

cos A × cot A = (√7/4) × (√7/3) = 7/12

**∴ The correct answer is 7/12.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6b0e696afd20f6169483e38f1c0e9c3d9e2b59cbb5f15f143254b96dffbfb18b.png] 

**Given:** sin A = 3/4

**Formula Used:** sin A = P/H, cos A = B/H, cot A = B/P, B = √(H² − P²)

⇒ P = 3, H = 4

⇒ B = √(4² − 3²) = √(16 − 9) = √7

⇒ cos A = B/H = √7/4

⇒ cot A = B/P = √7/3

⇒ Product = cos A × cot A = (√7/4) × (√7/3)

⇒ Product = 7/12

**∴ The correct answer is 7/12.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

Fundamental identity: sin²A + cos²A = 1. Therefore, cos A = √(1 − sin²A).

Pythagorean Triplet

For any right-angled triangle, (Perpendicular)² + (Base)² = (Hypotenuse)².

Ratio Relation

cot A can also be expressed as cos A / sin A. Thus, cos A × cot A = cos²A / sin A.</p

questions.question: If the manufacturer gains 10%, the wholesale gains 16% and the retailer gains 25%, then find the cost of production of a table (in ₹), whose retail price for the customer is ₹63,800. (NOTE: Manufacturer sells to wholesaler, wholesaler sells to retailer and retailer sells to customer.)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **cost of production** be x.

Retail price = x × (110 ÷ 100) × (116 ÷ 100) × (125 ÷ 100) = 63,800.

x × (11 ÷ 10) × (29 ÷ 25) × (5 ÷ 4) = 63,800.

x × (1595 ÷ 1000) = 63,800.

x = (63,800 × 1,000) ÷ 1,595 = 40,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹40,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → **Manufacturer Gain** = 10%, **Wholesaler Gain** = 16%, **Retailer Gain** = 25%, **Final Retail Price** = ₹63,800.
Formulas: SP = CP × (100 + P%) ÷ 100 | Successive CP Calculation.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6cba72780cde54e1e80ae5253385f7de2dcab4b9c9e38555e0b9b60dda201032.png] 
⇒ Price before Retailer = 63,800 × (100 ÷ 125) = 63,800 × (4 ÷ 5) = ₹51,040.
⇒ Price before Wholesaler = 51,040 × (100 ÷ 116) = ₹44,000.
⇒ Price before Manufacturer (Production Cost) = 44,000 × (100 ÷ 110) = ₹40,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹40,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Chain of Profit

When a product passes through multiple hands, the **Selling Price** of one becomes the **Cost Price** for the next. The final price is calculated using successive percentage increases.

Successive Percentage Formula

Net Increase = a + b + (a × b ÷ 100). This can be extended to three or more stages to find the overall markup from production to customer.
